name: Saturn from Voyager 2, June 19, 1981
blurb: The ringed planet, about 120,500 kilometers across at the equator. Seen by Voyager 2's narrow-angle camera through orange, green and violet filters: visible light only, 0.40 to 0.62 µm.
story: The whole of Saturn, fully lit, from about 64 million kilometers away, 68 days before Voyager 2's closest approach to Saturn on August 26, 1981. Its rings are billions of chunks of ice and rock, from dust-sized grains to pieces as big as a house.
